photo-color-adjuster.formula:
Exposure: v x 2^stops
Gamma: 255 x (v/255)^gamma
Hue: (h + shift) mod 360
Saturation: s x (amount/100)
Vibrance: s x (1 + v x (1 - s)), where v = (vibrance - 100)/100
howTo: Choose an image file (JPG, PNG, WebP up to 10 MB) from your device.
Move any slider — hue, saturation, vibrance, exposure, gamma or a color channel — and watch the live preview update.
Tick the compare box at any time to view the untouched original.
Use Reset all to return every slider to its neutral position.
Click Download PNG to save the adjusted photo to your device.
keyFacts: Exposure works in stops: +1 stop doubles brightness, -1 stop halves it.
Gamma below 1.0 brightens midtones, above 1.0 darkens them; 1.0 leaves the image unchanged.
Vibrance raises the saturation of dull colors first and protects already-saturated colors, which is why it is safer for skin tones than plain saturation.
Channel gains scale the red, green or blue channel independently from 0% to 200%.
Hue shift rotates every color around the color wheel from -180 to +180 degrees.

photo-color-adjuster.workedExample:
Take a mid-grey pixel at (128, 128, 128).
With exposure +1: each channel is multiplied by 2^1 = 2, so 128 x 2 = 256, which clamps to 255.
With gamma 2.0 instead: (128/255)^2 x 255 = 0.2519 x 255 = 64.2, which rounds to 64.
So the same grey pixel becomes near-white at +1 exposure, or a dark grey of 64 at gamma 2.0 — the math behind the sliders you see above.
